lesson: Weight alignment that predicted real parts: L24 MLP unit 7144 had .591 cosine to the mean month output direction and its ablation dropped month_offset by .3028 (control -.278), so month-name lexical support was real.

Fraction-role support was also real and more selective than raw fraction vocabulary: L22 unit 4840 dropped fraction_role by .1593 with only -.0099 on the control, and L21 unit 540 dropped fraction_role by .1915 with control -.1456.

For sign/product behavior, L15 attention head 1 was the best real hit: static OV directions preserved positive/negative tokens and ablation cut product_sign by .2016 while the matched control moved only .0253.

Some seemingly strong sign units failed specificity: L20 head 10 had clear positive/negative and (-/|- token structure in weights, but held-out check failed; its product_sign drop .189 was paired with a worse control (-.0524), so the candidate was not cleanly selective.

Pure weight clues were often misleading for MLP sign/delimiter clusters: L21 units 1194+8099 together gave product_sign .2373 but the control was .2156, L15 unit 1432 only .0812 vs .0126, and L27 delimiter units barely moved latex_superscript (.1092) with nearly the same control (.1058).
